messages:
maria: FYI — attaching this week's capacity readout. Short summary:
• EU-West trending +18% vs plan (sustained), headroom low for long sequences
• US-West demand spikes around batch jobs (nightly), preemptible churn high
• APAC healthy but monitoring increased latency in syd cluster

maria: Key numbers (rough):
```
Region   | curr_headroom | projected_peak_gpus | peak_gpu_hours_per_hr
EU-West  | 28            | 36                  | 72
US-West  | 15            | 50                  | 100
APAC     | 12            | 14                  | 28
Total est GPU-hrs this week: 12,800 (+9% vs last week)
```

sam: :eyes: Nice. EU-West 36 peak is worrying. Where are the long sequences coming from?

maria: Mostly from recommendation service A/B tests and a few large internal eval runs. We saw 3 eval runs yesterday that held KV caches for 2-3h each, which prevented reuse and bumped effective tokens/sec.

leo: Suggestion: enable per-route cache invalidation and cap long-running evals to a dedicated pool. If we offload evals to dedicated we can recover ~22% cost on the serving tier. Can canary tonight.

anya: Also noticed a handful of CI jobs hitting hosted endpoints with prod keys — PR to limit CI to dev cluster landed earlier. That should cut ~5% of the noise once deployed. I'll rollout today.

raul: Cost trade: moving 20% of bulk/embeddings to preemptible saves ~35% on those tokens (~$9k/week), but increases retry/error rate by ~6% based on last month. Need to be explicit which workloads tolerate retries.

sam: For user-facing low-latency routes avoid preemptibles. For evals/bulk embeddings it's acceptable. Action: mark evals -> dedicated-preemptible pool and set retry budget.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled eu-west-runtime +8 GPUs at 3162469300 (reason=cool_down_override)

maria: Draft plan for the next 72h:
1) Move evals to dedicated-preemptible pool (leo to own rollout).
2) Add temporary reserved +4 GPUs in EU-West to keep latency SLOs while we stabilize.
3) Apply route caps for nightly batch windows (sam + anya).
4) Update dashboards and cost forecast; alert on >90% baseline for >2h.

leo: I'll open the runbook PR for the eval migration and schedule the canary at 23:00 UTC.

sam: I'll prod the route caps later today and coordinate the canary window with leo.

anya: Rolling the CI key fix to prod now. ETA 45m.

maria: If nobody objects by EOD we proceed. I'll also ping Sales if SLA exposure risk exceeds 5% across EU customers. :thumbsup:

sam: +1 on the plan. One small ask — add a quick datadog query for the long-sequence traces so we can auto-flag next time. e.g.:
```
avg:trace.duration{service:redwood-runtime,env:prod} by {route} > 2m
```

maria: Good call — adding that to alerts. Thanks everyone.
thread_summary: Weekly capacity readout: EU-West demand spike, plan to offload evals to dedicated-preemptible pool, temporary reserved add in EU-West, route caps and CI key fix to reduce noise. Owners: leo (evals), sam+anya (route caps), maria (dashboard & sales ping).
